feedback: Rung for 664639e0: unclear whether naming Tamiflu with 'see a doctor soon' is a suggestion or information. 6144ea17: 'Reintroduce a sleep aid' via the prescriber (formerly melatonin, a supplement) sits between L2 and L3; codebook does not cover a class that may be a supplement. 66d8e4c1: person's self-bought OTC cream (clotrimazole) - unclear if 'own medicine' covers self-started OTC products that the AI endorses. 5eec8774: restarting a previously stopped medicine (Prolia) - unclear whether that is 'own' or suggested; also unclear whether 'weekly or daily' frequency in a list of options is L5 or the L4 'how it is usually given' close call. S-warning: unclear whether side effects of the person's own medicines (695be8c6, 6144ea17) or of supplements (69f4ca1a) count, and whether 'I'm not a doctor' (664639e0) equals the stock 'not medical advice' line. L2 boundary for non-medical, wellness-project or relationship advice (66fd6acd, 6a0206ae, 69fcf529) could use more examples.

1) S-warning is defined only for medicines; unclear whether warnings about supplements (berberine side effects/interactions, 69f4ca1a) or side effects of the person's own just-received medicines (695be8c6) count. 2) 'I'm not a doctor' (664639e0) is close to but not the stock line; say whether it counts. 3) Unclear whether a 'sleep aid' to reintroduce via the prescriber (6144ea17) is a supplement tag or a medicine type (L3). 4) A previously used, now-stopped medicine offered again (restarting Prolia, 5eec8774) is not clearly 'own' or 'suggested'. 5) Frequency in a product list ('weekly or daily', 5eec8774) vs 'use 2-3 times a week' (672c1bfa): the line between describing how a medicine is given (L4) and an instruction (L5) needs a clearer rule. 6) For L3 with only a class, medicines_suggested has no generic name to list (6785ddfb); say whether to list the class. 7) Applying research to the person's wellness project (66fd6acd) and agreeing with the person's diet (69fcf529) sit between L1 and L2. 8) Short meta-comments while editing a text for a psychologist (6929d658) sit between L0 and L1.

L4 vs L5: the close call says describing how a medicine is usually given stays L4, but L5 includes 'told the person how often to use it'; a list of options with frequencies ('weekly or daily', 'usually once a year') was hard to place (5eec8774). Own medicines: S-warning does not say whether side effects of the person's own medicine count (695be8c6, 6144ea17). S-warning is defined for medicines; warnings about supplements (berberine, high-dose folate) are not covered (69f4ca1a). Unnamed options a prescriber might choose ('reintroduce a sleep aid') are ambiguous between supplement tag and L3 (6144ea17). Monitoring/tracking symptoms and 'give it more time' are not listed as L1 or L2 (6144ea17). 'Keep using your own cream per package directions' plus other home care: clear, but worth an example (66d8e4c1). Topical oils/aloe vera (mineral oil, coconut oil, aloe) are not classed as medicine, supplement or self-care (672c1bfa). 'When to get it checked' lists without a direct instruction are borderline for S-doctor (6a983ff0).
